items.title: Fed expected to hold rates steady days ahead of US midterms
items.summary: The US Federal Reserve appears set to hold interest rates steady at its meeting next week, analysts say, despite stubbornly high inflation and with markets pricing in at least one rate hike before year-end. The Fed has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, and at its last meeting in September the FOMC voted to raise the key federal funds rate for the first time in three years, lifting the target range to 3.75 percent to 4.0 percent.

items.title: US consumer sentiment near record low ahead of midterm elections
items.summary: In October, consumer sentiment in the U.S. plummeted to a concerning 48.0, driven by rising prices and economic worries amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Survey results suggest that independents show the steepest drop in confidence, approaching historical lows. Additionally, inflation expectations have risen, marking a continuation of trends from earlier this year. Federal Reserve officials are attentively observing these shifts as they plan future interest rate adjustments.

items.title: Gold Loses Shine: Yellow Metal Prices Crash By Rs 9,700 In Just 10 Days, Fall Below Rs 1,42,000
items.summary: Gold prices have come under pressure as rising oil prices have revived concerns that persistent inflation could prompt the US Federal Reserve to keep interest rates higher for longer. This has reduced the appeal for non interest-bearing gold.
